title: Mastering Modern Layouts
subtitle: A Comprehensive Guide to CSS Flexbox

title: Introducing the Flexbox Model
bullets: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout model.
It provides an efficient way to distribute space among items in a container.
Key concepts include flex containers, flex items, and axes.

title: The Flex Container
body:
The flex container is the element that holds the flex items. 

To make an element a flex container, set its display property to flex or inline-flex. This enables flexbox behavior for its direct children, which become flex items.

title: Create Flex Container
description: Setting display: flex or display: inline-flex turns an element into a flex container.

title: Summary
bullets: Flexbox is a powerful layout tool.
The display property is key to enabling flexbox.
Understanding containers and items is fundamental.

title: Flex Items and Axes
body:
Flex items are the direct children of a flex container. 

They are arranged along the main axis, which is horizontal by default. The cross axis is perpendicular to the main axis.

title: Item Arrangement
description: These items will arrange horizontally by default.

title: Summary
bullets: Flex items are direct children of flex containers.
The main axis determines the primary direction of layout.
The cross axis is perpendicular to the main axis.

title: The Main Axis Property
body:
The main-axis property allows you to change the direction of the main axis. 

Common values include row (default), column, row-reverse, and column-reverse. This drastically changes how items are positioned.

title: Change Main Axis
description: Setting flex-direction: column causes the items to stack vertically

title: Summary
bullets: flex-direction controls the main axis.
row is the default, arranging items horizontally.
column arranges items vertically.

title: Controlling Flex Item Behavior
bullets: Flexbox provides properties to control item sizing, alignment, and order.
Understanding these properties is essential for creating complex layouts.
We'll explore flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, and align-items.

title: Flex Grow Property
body:
The flex-grow property specifies how much a flex item will grow relative to the other flex items in the container. 

It accepts a unitless value, where 0 means the item will not grow, and 1 means it will grow to fill available space. Higher values indicate a greater proportion of growth.

title: Flex Grow Example
description: Setting flex-grow: 1 on all items distributes space equally.

title: Summary
bullets: flex-grow determines how items expand.
A value of 1 means the item grows to fill available space.
Higher values indicate greater growth proportion.

title: Flex Shrink Property
body:
The flex-shrink property specifies how much a flex item will shrink relative to the other flex items in the container. 

It also accepts a unitless value, where 0 means the item will not shrink, and 1 means it will shrink to fit the container. Higher values mean a greater proportion of shrinking.

title: Flex Shrink Example
description: Items shrink if their content exceeds container width.

title: Summary
bullets: flex-shrink determines how items contract.
A value of 1 means the item will shrink to fit.
Higher values indicate a greater shrinking proportion.

title: Flex Basis Property
body:
The flex-basis property specifies the initial main size of a flex item. 

It can be a length (e.g., 100px) or a percentage (e.g., 50%). If not specified, the browser uses the item's width or height. The flex-basis property is the starting point for calculating the item's final size.

title: Flex Basis Example
description: Specifies the initial size of a flex item.

title: Summary
bullets: flex-basis sets the initial size of an item.
Can be specified in pixels, percentages, or other length units.
It's the starting point for size calculations.

title: Align Items Property
body:
The align-items property aligns flex items along the cross axis of the flex container. 

Common values include stretch (default), flex-start, flex-end, center, and baseline. This property affects the vertical alignment of items when the main axis is horizontal.

title: Align Items Example
description: Vertically aligns items within the flex container.

title: Summary
bullets: align-items controls cross-axis alignment.
stretch is the default, filling the container.
center aligns items to the center of the cross axis.

title: Putting Flexbox Into Practice
bullets: Learn to build real-world layouts with flexbox.
Explore techniques like wrapping, ordering, and justification.
Master responsive design using flexbox.

title: Flex Wrap Property
body:
The flex-wrap property specifies whether the flex items should wrap onto multiple lines if they exceed the container's width. 

Common values are nowrap (default), wrap, and wrap-reverse.  Wrapping is essential for creating responsive layouts that adapt to different screen sizes.

title: Enable Flex Wrap
description: Allows items to wrap to the next line.

title: Summary
bullets: flex-wrap controls whether items wrap.
nowrap is the default, keeping items on one line.
wrap allows items to flow to the next line.

title: Thank You for Learning Flexbox!
subtitle: Now go build some amazing layouts.
